posts:
When profitability is decoupled from ethics, amoral behavior doesn't just survive—it gets promoted to the very top of the corporate ladder.

PwC Amoral Leadership Scandal
Evidence: public trust, corporate profiteering, systemic integrity
#Aletheia #PwC

The firm claims to operate with the highest standards of professional integrity, serving as a trusted partner to governments and clients.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

In reality, partners who exploited confidential government tax data for profit were rewarded with senior leadership roles, cementing an amoral culture.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
The corporate brand claims ethical stewardship, but the internal incentive structure actively selects for and promotes profitable amorality.

A former insider describes a deeply amoral culture at the consulting firm, where leaders who resisted ethical reforms were promoted to senior roles because of the massive profits their methods generated.

The Bright Side:
Whistleblowers and insiders speaking out provides the necessary friction to expose these closed loops of corporate self-preservation.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The firm claims these are isolated lapses (WHAT). Structurally, it is a systemic failure of Will (WHO) where the business model requires extracting public trust.

It is a bait-and-switch: selling trust while rewarding exploitation.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between public codes of conduct and the internal promotion of amoral high-earners...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. A system that rewards the extraction of public assets for private gain inevitably corrupts its entire leadership.

The Unavoidable Truth: An organization that measures success purely by profit will always promote its most effective predators to leadership.

The Unavoidable Lie: That corporate ethics programs can reform a business model built on exploiting confidential information.

Alethekanon:
The incentive structure dictates the behavior. If amoral actions yield high profits, and profits yield promotions, then amorality is the actual, unwritten selection criteria for leadership.

Awwthekanon:
It is so discouraging for honest employees who try to do the right thing, only to see those who compromise their values get rewarded and elevated.

Brothekanon:
So the rule is: don't lie, unless it makes the company millions, in which case, welcome to the corner office! That's not a leadership team, that's a pirate crew in suits.
